istanbul_galataport_centre_about.note: Contact details are still being confirmed — ask at the terminal's own information desk when you arrive. Hours depend on the cruise schedule: it's generally open when a ship is in port, closed on days without one.

istanbul_galataport_centre_services.title: Services
istanbul_galataport_centre_services.note: Galataport is a modern cruise terminal with its own shops, cafés and information desks — being right in the city centre makes it easy to reach anything else you need.

istanbul_galataport_transport_taxi.title: Taxi

rows.title: Dedicated taxi rank right at the terminal exit

istanbul_galataport_transport_taxi.note: Always check the meter is running. Central Istanbul has heavy traffic, so a metered fare can end up higher than the app's initial estimate — that's normal, not a scam by itself.

rows.sub: To Sultanahmet (historic centre), Eminönü, Sirkeci

rows.title: İstanbulkart or a paper ticket
rows.sub: Bought at station machines · ~15–20 TRY

istanbul_galataport_transport_public.note: About 5 minutes to Sultanahmet. The tram runs until roughly midnight — after that, use a taxi.

callout.text: Never exchange money on the street, even for a good rate someone offers you. In some countries this is a criminal offence — and it's one of the most common ways seafarers get scammed near a port.

rows.title: A stranger offers you a better rate
rows.sub: On the street, at the gate, or "just around the corner" — always a scam

rows.title: Being asked to go somewhere private
rows.sub: A car, a back room, an alley — a legitimate exchange never needs this

rows.title: No receipt offered
rows.sub: A real exchange always gives you a printed receipt with the rate used

rows.title: Know the rough official rate first
rows.sub: Check on your phone before you go — so you can spot a bad deal immediately

rows.title: Count what you receive, before you walk away
rows.sub: In front of the person who gave it to you, not after
